properties.description:
`crates/reflow2-core/tests/heal.rs` — two checks holding `con:a-sweep-builds-its-network-a-fixed-number-of-times`.

`the_sweep_does_not_get_quadratically_slower_as_candidates_grow` builds two chains of components, 40 and 160 long. Every interior node of a chain is an articulation point, so candidates scale directly with length — which is what makes the test measure the thing the budget is about. It asserts a RATIO under 10x for a 4x size increase.

⚠️ A RATIO, NOT A THRESHOLD, DELIBERATELY. Both halves run on the same machine under the same load, so contention cancels. A bare millisecond bound here would measure the test runner, and the standing response to that is to raise it until it stops complaining — which retires a gate without anybody deciding to. The bar is 10x rather than 1x because 4x the nodes IS genuinely more work: more edges to walk, more nodes to scan. What it forbids is that cost growing with candidates ON TOP of that.

`masking_a_node_gives_the_same_verdict_as_rebuilding_without_it` is the correctness half: on a 5-chain the ends are not single points of failure and the middle is. The optimisation replaced "rebuild the network without this node and recount" with "mask this node in the network already built", and those must agree.

⭐ THE REAL GUARD IS THE TYPE SIGNATURE AND THIS TEST GUARDS WHAT A SIGNATURE CANNOT. The old `is_single_point_of_failure(&self, node_id)` could rebuild because it held `&self`. The new `is_single_point_of_failure_in(&DesignNetwork, baseline, node_id)` is handed the network and has no graph to rebuild from, so the per-candidate cost cannot return inside that function. What it CAN do is return at the call site, by hoisting nothing and calling in a loop — which is exactly what the ratio test catches.

MUTATION-CHECKED, and it bites hard. Putting the per-candidate rebuild back at the call site fails the ratio check at **19.8x** with a message naming the constraint: \"4x the candidates cost 19.8x the time (0.259s -> 5.132s) — the network is being rebuilt per candidate again\". Restoring passes 50 of 50. A guard seen only green is indistinguishable from one that cannot fail.
properties.findings:
2026-08-21. 50 of 50 heal tests pass, whole core suite green, 0 failures.

MEASURED ON reflow2'S OWN DESIGN (2871 nodes), in-memory debug, before and after:

  detect_structural_defects   44.50s  ->   4.43s
  all_defects                 56.32s  ->  16.65s
  is_single_point_of_failure  878ms PER CANDIDATE  ->  5.08ms for ALL 56
  defects found                   54  ->      54   (unchanged)
  structural issues               13  ->      13   (unchanged)

ON THE PATH USERS ACTUALLY TAKE — release binary, real RocksDB, driven over stdio through the real tool surface:

  open_questions   11.7s -> 2.95s     <= the FIRST call of every session
  loop_status      11.4s -> 2.50s
  graph_report     10.9s -> 2.18s warm
  detect_gaps      0.51s -> 0.53s     (untouched, as expected)
  get_node/scan_nodes unchanged

AGAINST THE BUDGET, WHICH IS WHAT DECIDES WHETHER TO STOP: `con:a-sweep-builds-its-network-a-fixed-number-of-times` allows 4 network builds per sweep, independent of candidates. Now 3 — two design networks and one operational network. UNDER BUDGET, SO THE WORK STOPPED.

DELIBERATELY LEFT UNDONE, and each would be a further gain: `sweep_scope` is now the largest remaining part (15.3s of ~32s in-memory), of which `rule_populations` is 9.1s; and `design_network` is still built TWICE per sweep — once in `sweep_scope`, once in `detect_structural_defects` — which sharing would remove. Both are inside budget, so they stop here rather than being taken because they are visible. Reopening them wants its own measurement and its own number.

MUTATION-CHECKED: restoring the per-candidate rebuild fails the ratio check at 19.8x and names the constraint in the message.
properties.name: Four times the candidates does not cost four times the sweep, and masking a node gives the same verdict as rebuilding without it
